findings.text: Tested on an emulated FM-1 with the newer UC25HQ80 flash chip: it uses its flash the same way as on the original chip, so settings save and later installs work on newer FM-1 units.

From the code alone: Checks for the original Puya flash chip only. On newer FM-1 units (UC25HQ80 flash) firmware like this has kept saves in RAM only and refused later installs, which then needs a USB download-mode rescue. Check the project's notes for newer-unit support before installing on a recent FM-1.
Contains the chip's standard Bluetooth/networking libraries (as M-VAVE's own firmware does); no sign it talks to internet servers.
Does not pose as a keyboard, mouse or drive over USB.

brick.reason: Uses its flash the same way on the UC25HQ80 (331 storage operations vs 331 on the original chip).
